# FPGA 101 workshop (`mmicko__fpga101-workshop`)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Upstream | https://github.com/mmicko/fpga101-workshop |

| HDL / framework | Verilog (82 files), C firmware and a MicroPython port, 2 IceStudio designs |

| Target FPGA(s) | iCE40 UP5K SG48 (NOT ECP5), 12 MHz clock (`pinout.pcf`) |
| Board revision(s) | FPGA101 badge of Hackaday Belgrade 2018 (parallel RGB LCD, RGB LED, buttons, audio out) |

## What the gateware does

A progressive FPGA course in 20 exercises, each a small apio project (`top.v` + `pinout.pcf` + `apio.ini`), from a blinking LED to a RISC-V SoC running MicroPython, plus a complete Galaksija retro computer. It is the **original of several ULX3S resources**: the same author's ULX3S workshop [ulx3s__fpga-odysseus](https://github.com/ulx3s/fpga-odysseus) shares 10 identical files (grom CPU, i8080/Altair computer, UARTs), and the toy "grom" CPU found in lawrie's ULX3S and ULX4M examples is this one ([lawrie__ulx3s_examples review](lawrie__ulx3s_examples.md)). The Galaksija project is the upstream of emard__galaksija and emard__ulx3s_galaksija.

## Structure

- `tutorials/`: the 20 exercises above; each directory is a standalone apio project.
- `projects/galaksija/`: complete retro computer (`tv80*.v`, `video.v`, `font_rom.v`, `rom_memory.v`).
- `tests/`: environment checks from the README.
- `presentation/`: workshop slides (pptx/pdf, removed from the local clone by pruning; available upstream).

## How to build

As found in the README (not run here):

```bash
cd tutorials/02-LED
apio build      # yosys synth_ice40 -> arachne-pnr -d 5k -P sg48 -> icepack
apio sim        # opens GTKWave on the testbench, where one exists
cd tutorials/12-RiscV/01-Simple && make   # RISC-V firmware
```

The exercises assume the FPGA101 badge (`apio.ini`: `board = fpga101`); arachne-pnr is obsolete, nextpnr-ice40 (`--up5k --package sg48`) is the modern equivalent.

## Reuse notes

| Block | Path | Top module | Language | Vendor primitives | License |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| grom toy CPU + computer | `tutorials/10-CPU/` | `grom_top` | Verilog | none | MIT (repo) |
| i8080 Altair computer | `tutorials/11-Computer/` | `top` (in `top_altair.v`) / `altair` | Verilog | SB_HFOSC (top only) | i8080 modified BSD; rest MIT |
| PicoSoC + LCD text console | `tutorials/12-RiscV/` | `top` | Verilog | SB_SPRAM256KA, SB_PLL40_CORE, SB_IO, SB_HFOSC | MIT; PicoRV32 ISC |
| Parallel LCD video timing | `tutorials/05-Video/00-Basic/video.v` | `video` | Verilog | none (PLL in `lcd_pll.v`) | MIT (repo) |
| Galaksija | `projects/galaksija/` | `top` | Verilog | SB_SPRAM256KA, SB_PLL40_CORE, SB_HFOSC | MIT; TV80 own license |

- For ULX3S, start from [ulx3s__fpga-odysseus](https://github.com/ulx3s/fpga-odysseus) rather than porting: it is the same author's ULX3S version of these exercises (DVI instead of the LCD, ECP5 PLL).
- Porting a single exercise: replace `SB_PLL40_CORE`/`SB_HFOSC` with the 25 MHz `clk_25mhz` and an `EHXPLLL`, and `SB_SPRAM256KA` with block RAM or SDRAM ([porting guide](../guides/porting-ice40-to-ecp5.md)).
- Cores recorded on the site: [grom CPU](../functions/cpu-retro.md), [PicoSoC with MicroPython](../functions/cpu-riscv.md).
